caption:
Highland clay in Costa Rica has a memory of its own. When the afternoon mist rolls over the ridge, the trail transforms from a firm track into a patient test of traction and cadence. Mountain biking in Costa Rica is rarely about pure speed; it is about finding grip where none seems to exist, letting the climb dictate your pace, and trusting your legs. Up here, far above the highway, the silence is absolute—broken only by the breath in your lungs and the soft slip of tires on wet earth.
